pageCache.text:
academicexcellence,Personal Success
Welcome
I would like to welcome you to the Weald of Kent Grammar School. We are a happy, purposeful and vibrant school community with a reputation for high academic standards.
Academic excellence
At Weald of Kent, we are committed to delivering a curriculum of consistent exceptional quality of education. To do so, we ensure that our curriculum intent and implementation are embedded securely and consistently across the school.
Inspiring enthusiasm
At Weald of Kent, we have a clear understanding of our students’ potential and abilities, and therefore their cultural capital that needs to be broadened to play an active part in our modern and fast-evolving world. As a result, we are offering a variety of opportunities that we consider as “essential knowledge that our students need to acquire to become educated citizens, introducing them to the best that has been thought and said, and helping to engender an appreciation of human creativity and achievement.”
The brightest of futures
Providing a stimulating, well-equipped academic learning environment is critical to the development of our progressive curriculum and success. We continually strive to enhance our facilities for all students.

pageCache.pageTitle: Guest Speakers - Weald of Kent Grammar School
pageCache.text:
Guest Speakers
We regularly invite guest speakers into school to inspire students and take them beyond the curriculum. For our sixth formers, these talks can provide valuable insights into university courses and careers.
Recent speakers have included live online lectures from Durham University on Black History and The Sociology of Egyptian Mythology, Goldsmiths University on The Sociological History of the Pink Pound, a Criminology lecturer from University of Kent, a Professor of Psychology from Kings College London on the Psychology of Health Scares, and a writer specialising in Queer History in Gothic Literature. During Science Week we welcomed a Research Fellow from the University of Portsmouth who gave an insight into palaeontology fieldwork in Brazil.
Media Studies students have enjoyed talks by Zoe Duerden, an edit producer for programmes such as The Traitors, Love Island and Gogglebox; Helen Ostler, a producer on The Last Kingdom and second director on Killing Eve, Fleabag and Rev; and Martin Webber, a BBC World Service journalist. We have also had online lectures about Media Production from Ravensbourne University, and about music videos from the BFI.

Music and Drama
Music and Drama opportunities are provided beyond the curriculum in the form of extracurricular clubs. These include Junior and Senior Choir, Orchestra and Flute Choir, and Drama clubs. The annual Weald Variety Show, performed at the EM Forster Theatre, is a wonderful showcase of talent from Year 7 to Year 13 and includes solo and group musical performances, musical theatre numbers and dramatic pieces. Concerts, such as the summer and Christmas concerts, are highlights of the school year and features musical ensembles and solo performers.

Computer Science
The intention of the Computer Science curriculum at Weald of Kent Grammar School is to inspire students to go on to become leading experts in the computer science field. We teach practical skills such as computer programming which are in high demand in an ever changing world and allow students to go directly into jobs and apprenticeships. However, for those students who choose not to pursue careers in computer science, the intention is to equip them with knowledge, skills and understanding that will prepare them for a living and working in a technological world.

pageCache.pageTitle: Music - Weald of Kent Grammar School
pageCache.text:
Music
Music is the language of sound, it exists in time and space. Perhaps the broadest definition of music is that it is organised sound (and silence!) Understanding music requires both the understanding of conventions and the challenging of them; ‘Works of Art make rules; rules do not make works of art’ Claude Debussy.
All activities in music lessons are designed to create or experience sound. This is achieved through almost exclusively practical tasks, being as true in year 7 as it is in year 13.
The journey between these two points is one of exploring how sound has been and can be organised in order to create an intended effect. Students demonstrate their understanding of this through integrated activities of listening performing and composing.

pageCache.pageTitle: Equality, Diversity and Inclusion - Weald of Kent Grammar School
pageCache.text:
Equality, Diversity and Inclusion
The purpose of the Equality, Diversity and Inclusion activities at Weald are:
To create a positive school culture EDI promotes a culture of respect, understanding, and acceptance. It fosters a sense of community where students and staff feel valued and appreciated, leading to better outcomes for everyone. To promote a sense of belonging We want to help students and staff feel like they belong, leading to better mental health and wellbeing. Students who feel like they belong are more likely to attend school regularly and have better outcomes. Schools whose staff feel like they belong have higher retention rates and lower absenteeism.
To improve academic performance When students feel included and valued, they are more likely to engage in their learning and perform better academically. Teachers who value diversity are more likely to create an inclusive curriculum that meets the needs of all students.
To prepare students for the future In today's global society, it's essential to prepare students to live and work in diverse environments. By promoting EDI at Weald, we can equip students with the skills they need to thrive in an increasingly interconnected world.
A number of events take place over the school year. Often these are student-led, but we have also welcomed a number of external providers and speakers to Weald. Events have included special assemblies on European Day of Languages, Black History Month, Diwali, Holocaust Memorial Week, LGBT+ History Month, Ramadam and International Women's Day. Black History Month also encompassed bake sales, themed lunches and South African dance and language cultural workshops.
The Weald International Film Festival was a Year 9 Enrichment Day activity that provided scope for a host of cross-curricular activities. The students watched films on the theme of 'children of courage' in French, German, Spanish and Japanese at the Stag Theatre in Sevenoaks. Students were invited to consider people with autism and disabilities, refugees and illegal migrants from a different perspective. To supplement this, the History and Geography departments led cross-curricular sessions on migration in Mexico, Resistance Groups in Nazi Germany and Kindertransport in the Holocaust. The day was designed to promote the values of internationalism, empathy and resilience, as well as practising GCSE speaking skills in French, Spanish and German.

pageCache.pageTitle: Learning Support - Weald of Kent Grammar School
pageCache.text:
Learning Support
At the Weald of Kent we are committed to ensuring that the needs of our students with SEND are understood and met through inclusive practice. The Learning Support Team work closely with these students and pastoral staff to support and empower, removing barriers to learning through an inclusive curriculum which is tailored to the needs of all of our students. This work is strongly underpinned by high quality teaching and all staff understand the pivotal role that they play in creating a supportive environment. The Learning Support Team have expertise in the four key areas of need and take a personalised approach, understanding how factors may impact our students in different ways and change over time. We are fully invested in our motto, ‘the whole child is our whole point’ and we maintain a whole-school approach to inclusive practice and pedagogy and prioritise support and training with our staff to achieve this goal.

pageCache.pageTitle: ESAA English Schools' Track & Field Cup 2026 - Weald of Kent Grammar School
pageCache.text:
ESAA English Schools' Track & Field Cup 2026
Congratulations to the athletes who represented Weald at the Regional 'A' Final of the ESAA Schools Cup, which was held at Medway Park, Gillingham on Wednesday 17th June.
The Junior Girls team finished in a very respectable 7th place with 315 points behind some of the nation's top performing schools. Croydon High School took the overall win with 478 points, with Guildford High School 2nd and St Catherines School in 3rd. Our top points scorers came from the middle-distance trio Cora earning a huge 26 points running 2.34 and Aria recording a personal best time of 2.41 coming away with 24 points in the 800m. Rosie gained 23 points in the 1500m, posting a new lifetime best of 5.40. A huge congratulations to Georgie who set a very impressive personal best in the shot recording a huge throw of 7.87m for 20 points. Florence led the way for the sprints team with an impressive 29.2 points for the 200m. The relay team came home in second place with a fantastic display of teamwork from Martha, Jasmine, Georgie, and Elysia.
Congratulation to the whole Junior team who showed dedication, excellent sportsmanship, positive attitudes and served as excellent ambassadors for the school. Well done!

pageCache.pageTitle: Poetry and Art Celebration Event 2026 - Weald of Kent Grammar School
pageCache.text:
Poetry and Art Celebration Event 2026
The Weald of Kent Poet Laureates, Maxine, Isla and Lara (year 10) from Tonbridge and Leia and Lexie (Year 9) and Pranshi (Year 10) from Sevenoaks led a wonderful Poetry and Art Celebration evening at the Sevenoaks campus on Wednesday evening. The event highlighted the incredible poetry written and performed by Weald students this year. In addition, poems and artwork produced by students for our competition on the theme of ‘Light’ was showcased during the evening. Selected poems and art will appear in an Anthology, a copy of which will be given to each of the featured poets and artists.
The evening began with some beautiful music performed by Sevenoaks students on the grand piano while parents, students and teachers mingled and enjoyed the art exhibition. The Poet Laureates then introduced the evening and invited poets to perform their work, whilst related art pieces were displayed.
In addition to poems from the competition, students performed poems that they had written for a national competition led by Poet Laureate Simon Armitage to locate regional poets in KS2 and KS3 from across the country. Caitlin’s poem was Commended in that competition and Eloise’s poem ‘Nerd’ was a finalist. Two Year 10 students also performed published poems, ‘When We Two Parted’ and ‘Remains’ which they had entered for the National Poetry By Heart Competition.
Finally, there was an awards ceremony for poems judged by published author and poet Nathalie Abi-Ezzi and artwork judged by the Weald Art Department. The standard of art and poetry was stunning and demonstrates the talents of Weald students.

pageCache.pageTitle: Year 12 Biology Trip to Flatford Mills - Weald of Kent Grammar School
pageCache.text:
Year 12 Biology Trip to Flatford Mills
For the whole week starting Monday the 8th of June, the biology department visited Flatford Mill which is recognised for housing the famous artist John Constable and its vast biodiversity with ponds, forests and fields. Throughout the trip, we explored a variety of habitats and carried out practical investigations to deepen our understanding of ecology.
One of our main activities involved studying ponds and lakes, where we identified and compared a wide range of aquatic species. It was fascinating to discover and capture organisms that many of us had never encountered before and to learn how they contribute to their ecosystems.
We also conducted research in forest habitats, investigating plant life and measuring species abundance. These activities helped us understand how biodiversity can vary within an ecosystem and the factors that influence it. This also allowed us to plan and conduct our own experiment later in the trip.
A particular highlight was our visit to a salt marsh. Despite being caught in a storm, it was a memorable experience that allowed us to observe a unique habitat and the specialised halophytes that live there. The challenging weather certainly made the trip more adventurous!
There was plenty of laughs shared as we navigated the rain in oversized waterproofs and wellies, creating memories that will last long after the trip and photos that definitely won’t be forgotten!
Overall, the field trip was both educational and exciting. It provided valuable hands-on experience, strengthened our understanding of ecology which will benefit our studies into year 13, and gave us the opportunity to appreciate the incredible diversity of life in different environments around us.
Rosie and Millie, Year 12 Biologists

Free 11+ resources for Pupil Premium children
To encourage even greater representation of children at Weald of Kent, we work in partnership with Atom Learning, the leading online 11+ preparation platform, to provide students who are eligible for pupil premium and sitting the Kent Test with free online exam preparation materials.
This programme is designed to help familiarise children with the questions they may see on the Kent Test, and build exam technique and confidence ahead of their 11+.
If your child is in Years 3 - 6 and has been eligible for free school meals at any point in the last six years, please fill in the form by clicking the button below. They will be given free access to Atom Home when their pupil premium status has been verified by their primary school.
